newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki exchanges say not discussing Nordic link.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki exchanges say not discussing Nordic link.

text.p: A planned merger between the Helsinki bourse and derivatives exchange SOM Oy will strengthen their position internationally but the merging exchanges said on Tuesday they were not now discussing a Nordic link-up.

"The future is the future, and we believe that with what we have now we will be a strong partner," Juha Korhonen, chairman of SOM Oy told a news conference after the two said they plan to merge into a single company by year-end.
"(But) at this time we are not engaged in any negotiations in any direction," he added.
The stock exchange and SOM said they would merge into a new company called HEX Oy, which will be registered by the end of this year, but would begin integrated operations immediately.
"One-stop shopping or single entry (into the Finnish financial market) is one very concrete goal of the coordinated operations," Korhonen said.
"We have been watching with interest what has been happening in neighbouring countries on the bourse front," he said.

"This (merger) will strengthen Helsinki's position as a marketplace," said Ossi Virolainen, chairman of the Helsinki Stock Exchange. He added that the reinforced position would be a benefit "regardless of what happens around us."

The international trend is clearly toward mergers of spot and derivatives trading, said stock exchange president and CEO Juhani Erma, pointing to recent developments in the Netherlands, Switzerland, Germany and Denmark.
"(But) we've chosen not to go for complex or difficult solutions that would tie our hands, but rather to seek cooperation by trying to network with other possible cooperation partners," Erma said.

Swedish derivatives exchange OM Gruppen, with a 15.7 percent stake in the new group, would be a very significant owner, but had no special role to play as far as a Nordic ownership link-up was concerned, Korhonen said.

However, trading cooperating with OM Gruppen aimed at making Finnish derivatives available abroad and making OM's Swedish derivatives available in Finland from the start of next year, said SOM managing director Asko Schrey.
The improved cost efficiency to be gained by uniting operations would benefit customers, Virolainen added.
